pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What instrument measures the volume of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Beam balance
   B. Ruler
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Stopwatch

2. Which state of matter is used in a cooking gas cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Ice
   C. Solid
   D. Powder

3. Which of these is true of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. It fills a room
   B. It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   C. It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume
   D. It has no volume

4. There are 750 ml of milk in a jug. 300 ml is poured out. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 450 ml
   B. 1050 ml
   C. 550 ml
   D. 350 ml

5. Which unit is used for the mass of a sack of maize? (1 mark)
   A. Kilogram
   B. Metre
   C. Litre
   D. Second

6. What is decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Waste made of plastic
   B. Waste that rots and breaks down
   C. Waste that never changes
   D. Waste made of metal

7. Why is waste in rivers dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water dirty and harms fish
   B. It makes water clean
   C. It makes rain
   D. It makes fish bigger

8. What does the word biodegradable mean? (1 mark)
   A. Made of glass
   B. Not able to rot
   C. Able to be broken down by living things
   D. Made of plastic

9. A pupil wants to make a toy car from waste. Which materials are suitable? (1 mark)
   A. Fire and paper
   B. Water and air
   C. Banana peel and leaves
   D. A box and bottle tops

10. Which disease can spread by mosquitoes breeding in old tins that hold water? (1 mark)
   A. Diarrhoea only
   B. Malaria
   C. Toothache
   D. Sunburn

11. Which living things help waste to decompose? (1 mark)
   A. Fungi and bacteria
   B. Bottles
   C. Plastic bags
   D. Stones

12. What is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Dirty water
   B. Smoke from a fire
   C. Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   D. Air from a tyre

13. Which is an example of reusing? (1 mark)
   A. Burning a plastic bottle
   B. Throwing it in a drain
   C. Using a washed bottle to carry water
   D. Leaving it on the road

14. Which of these is NOT a way of managing solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing it in a river
   B. Composting
   C. Reusing
   D. Recycling

15. Which of these can be made from waste for the classroom? (1 mark)
   A. A new mountain
   B. A house
   C. A car engine
   D. A dustbin

16. How does mulching help save water? (1 mark)
   A. It makes soil hot
   B. It makes water flow away
   C. It makes soil dry
   D. It reduces evaporation from the soil

17. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. A leaking tap wastes 40 litres in a day. How many jerrycans is that? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 4
   C. 20
   D. 60

18. Why should we not throw waste in rivers? (1 mark)
   A. It pollutes the water
   B. It makes water clean
   C. It helps fish
   D. It makes water sweet

19. What should you do when you see a leaking tap at school? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Open it wider
   C. Play with it
   D. Tell an adult so it can be fixed

20. What is rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Catching and storing rainwater
   B. Selling rainwater
   C. Drinking rainwater from puddles
   D. Digging wells

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Group these into solid, liquid and gas: milk, chalk, oxygen, cooking oil, book, steam. (4 marks)

22. Describe how you can show that a liquid takes the shape of its container. (3 marks)

23. Why should you wear gloves when collecting waste? (2 marks)

24. Explain how a school can manage waste at the kitchen, classrooms and playground. (4 marks)

25. Describe how kitchen waste can be turned into manure. (3 marks)

26. What is meant by water conservation? (2 marks)

27. Describe two properties of a liquid. (3 marks)

28. Give two ways of reducing waste at home. (2 marks)

29. Name the three Rs of waste management. (2 marks)

30. Plan a project to sensitise your community about the importance of water conservation. State the steps. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Measuring jug
   A measuring jug or cylinder shows volume.

2. A — Gas
   Cooking gas is a gas that burns to give heat.

3. B — It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   A liquid has a fixed volume and takes the container's shape.

4. A — 450 ml
   750 - 300 = 450 ml.

5. A — Kilogram
   Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

6. B — Waste that rots and breaks down
   Decomposable waste is broken down by decomposers.

7. A — It makes water dirty and harms fish
   Waste pollutes water and harms living things.

8. C — Able to be broken down by living things
   Biodegradable waste rots naturally.

9. D — A box and bottle tops
   A box and bottle tops make a toy car.

10. B — Malaria
   Mosquitoes spread malaria and breed in standing water.

11. A — Fungi and bacteria
   Decomposers such as fungi and bacteria break down waste.

12. C — Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   Solid waste is unwanted solid material.

13. C — Using a washed bottle to carry water
   The bottle is used again for a new purpose.

14. A — Throwing it in a river
   Throwing waste in rivers pollutes water.

15. D — A dustbin
   A dustbin can be made from waste materials like a bucket or box.

16. D — It reduces evaporation from the soil
   Covered soil stays moist longer.

17. A — 2
   40 divided by 20 = 2.

18. A — It pollutes the water
   Waste makes water dirty and unsafe.

19. D — Tell an adult so it can be fixed
   Reporting leaks helps save water.

20. A — Catching and storing rainwater
   Harvesting means collecting rainwater from roofs.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: chalk and book. Liquids: milk and cooking oil. Gases: oxygen and steam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 200 ml of water into a tall glass and then into a wide bowl. The shape of the water changes but the amount stays the same.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two containers, 1 mark for shape changing, 1 mark for the volume the same.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect your hands from cuts and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cuts and 1 mark for germs.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kitchen: compost pit for food waste and separate bin for plastic. Classroom: bin with lid and paper box. Playground: bins and monitors who pick litter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each place and 1 mark for a clear system.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put peelings and other kitchen waste with dry leaves and some soil in a compost pit. Decomposers rot it and after some weeks it turns to compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the pit, 1 mark for decomposers, 1 mark for compost.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Using water carefully and protecting water sources so that there is enough for everyone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for careful use and 1 mark for protecting or enough for everyone.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: A liquid has a fixed volume and no shape of its own. It takes the shape of its container and can be poured.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of two properties and 1 mark for the example.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Buy less packaging, carry a reusable bag, cook only what is needed, repair things.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

30. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a message, make posters, put them near taps and gates, speak at assembly, do a demonstration of saving water and check results.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.
